available_assertion.statement: A unitary cuspidal pi with pi not isomorphic to pi tensor eta has a unique sigma-stable cuspidal weak lift Pi over L.
available_assertion.objects: L/K cyclic prime degree q; pi on GL(n,A_K); eta generates the characters of K*Norm(A_L*)\A_K*.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such prime cyclic extension and unitary cuspidal pi.
available_assertion.hypotheses: pi is not isomorphic to pi tensor eta.
available_assertion.parameter_range: n positive; q any prime, including 2.
available_assertion.uniformity: Existence and uniqueness for each fixed extension and representation; no quantitative bounds.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: The self-twist case is a different part of the theorem and is not included in this conclusion.
available_assertion.constants: Degree q; unramified residue degree f.
available_assertion.normalization: Weak lift raises unitary Satake matrices to their f-th powers.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix L/K and pi before applying III4.2(a).

needed_assertion.statement: The weight-two cuspidal form attached to r|G_K has a cuspidal lift attached to the same r|G_L.
needed_assertion.objects: n=2; K,L totally real; l-adic r with nonsolvable residual image throughout the selected solvable tower.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Every prime step in that tower at which r|G_K is modular.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: The stable lattice and solvable top extension imply residual and characteristic-zero absolute irreducibility on G_L. U04 supplies attachment.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: The coefficient prime l may be 2 and is distinct from the tower degree variable q.
needed_assertion.uniformity: One fixed global r is used at all steps.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: A self-twist forces eta squared equal to 1. Odd q is impossible by determinant; q=2 gives two G_L-stable eigenspaces in characteristic zero, also impossible.
needed_assertion.constants: Arithmetic roots alpha,beta have product q_v*s_v; q_w=q_v^f.
needed_assertion.normalization: Unitary roots divide by sqrt(q_v); their f-th powers restore arithmetic roots alpha^f,beta^f.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Exclude the self-twist first, apply III4.2(a), recover weight via split places, then compare attached representations.

comparisons.comparison: III4.2 explicitly assumes q prime; the solvable tower is refined to such steps.
Weight-two Hilbert forms are used in unitary cuspidal normalization, matching Definition4.1.
The non-self-twist condition is proved from the same target r by the determinant and quadratic-eigenspace arguments.
Use part(a), not merely existence part(c), so the resulting lift is cuspidal.
Unramified Satake powers and U04 identify the arithmetic representation with r restricted to G_L.
The intertwiner is in characteristic zero even when l=2; q denotes the extension degree.
III5.1 at split real places supplies weight, not weak lifting alone.
The q=2 obstruction is explicitly ruled out; no induction exception is silently omitted.
No composite descent, general local parameter comparison or global degree bound is used.

available_assertion.statement: A sigma-stable unitary cuspidal Pi over L descends to a cuspidal pi over K; its q descendants differ by eta powers.
available_assertion.objects: L/K cyclic prime degree q; Pi on GL(n,A_L); generator sigma and norm character eta.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every invariant unitary cuspidal Pi in this prime-degree setting.
available_assertion.hypotheses: Pi is isomorphic to Pi composed with sigma.
available_assertion.uniformity: One-step existence and fiber statement only.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No composite-degree invariant descent is claimed.
available_assertion.normalization: The descent is a weak lift with the same unramified Satake-power convention.

needed_assertion.statement: There is a weight-two cuspidal descendant whose attached representation equals r|G_K after the uniquely needed finite-character correction.
needed_assertion.objects: Pi is attached to r|G_L; r is already defined on G_K; both restrictions have dimension two.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Every downward prime step in the fixed solvable tower.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: Absolute irreducibility on G_L; invariance follows from global r and III(2.4); split infinity gives weight two; U04 supplies the descendant attachment.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: q any prime and coefficient l any prime; finite coefficient extensions allowed.
needed_assertion.uniformity: The target is the restriction of the same original r at each step.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: A raw descendant need not already have the target determinant or equal r; its difference is the scalar character chi of Gal(L/K).
needed_assertion.constants: chi has finite order dividing q.
needed_assertion.normalization: If R=r tensor chi, twist the automorphic form by the inverse arithmetic-reciprocity Hecke character of chi.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Choose a descendant, compare G_L restrictions, obtain chi by Schur, correct it, then re-establish invariance for the next step.

comparisons.comparison: Global r supplies conjugation invariance; III(2.4) converts all unramified Hecke equalities to Pi^sigma=Pi.
Only the printed prime-degree part(d) is invoked.
Part(d) supplies a cuspidal descendant, rather than a possibly Eisenstein object.
The real places split, and III5.1 preserves their exact weight-two components.
Finite central character plus that weight supplies the retained U04 domain.
Both restrictions to G_L are the same absolutely irreducible two-dimensional representation.
Their scalar ratio defines chi of Gal(L/K); inverse arithmetic Hecke twist gives exactly r.
At the next step start with the corrected form and verify its invariance anew.
No arbitrary intermediate descendant is assumed invariant, avoiding the defect of III6.3.

available_assertion.statement: In the prime-degree setting of III4.2, a weak lift between representations induced from unitary cuspidal ones is a strong lift.
available_assertion.objects: pi on GL(n,A_K), Pi on GL(n,A_L); local components at every place.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every such weak lift for the fixed prime cyclic L/K.
available_assertion.hypotheses: Both representations are induced from cuspidal in Definition4.1; they satisfy weak lifting.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Every place; this application consumes only split real places.
available_assertion.uniformity: Local identity for each place, without quantitative uniformity.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not confuse local Lemma I.6.3 with composite descent Lemma III.6.3.
available_assertion.constants: At a split place L tensor K_v is K_v^q.
available_assertion.normalization: I.5 transfer is convolution; the Galois action permutes factors and lifting repeats the local component.
available_assertion.limit_order: Obtain the global weak lift before using III5.1.

needed_assertion.statement: The cuspidal lift and descendant in H-D4 have the same weight-two real components; the descendant central character has finite order.
needed_assertion.objects: K,L totally real; each real completion gives L tensor K_v=R^q.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Every real place in every prime step.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: The lift is weak and cuspidal; the split-place consequence of III5.1 applies. Class-field/ray-class finiteness is retained.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: Only split real local behavior is consumed.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Parallel weight two is preserved across the finite tower.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: No general ramified local Galois/LLC comparison is inferred from this assertion.
needed_assertion.constants: Central character is trivial on positive real groups and smooth of some finite conductor.
needed_assertion.normalization: Split convolution and cyclic tensor trace identify equal local representations, not an unspecified Tate or absolute-value twist.
needed_assertion.limit_order: First identify real components; then use conductor plus finite ray-class quotient to obtain finite central character.

comparisons.comparison: III5.1 carries the prime-degree assumptions of III4.2.
Both sides here are cuspidal and hence fall within induced-from-cuspidal scope.
Both number fields are totally real, so every real completion splits as R^q.
I.5 identifies split transfer with convolution of the component test functions.
Cyclic tensor trace and independence identify the actual local representation.
No unramified norm twist arises at a split real place.
Its real connected restriction is trivial and its finite conductor is open, so the ray-class quotient is finite.
I.6.3 is the local lemma; III6.3 is excluded. The split calculation does not require the non-split local classification.
Only infinity weight and central-character domain are adopted; the separate ramified local-BC bridge remains separate.

available_assertion.statement: Cuspidal pairs on Levi subgroups of GL(n) with equal unramified Hecke conjugacy classes at almost all places are conjugate.
available_assertion.objects: The cuspidal Levi pairs (M,pi),(L,sigma) in III(2.4).
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every two such pairs over the same number field and same total n.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Unitary cuspidal factors as in III2.
available_assertion.uniformity: An exact uniqueness statement; finite exceptional sets may vary.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Equal data only at split primes are not asserted sufficient here.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical density bound; equality is outside a finite set.
available_assertion.normalization: Hecke matrices use the unitary normalization of III2.

needed_assertion.statement: Pi is isomorphic to Pi composed with sigma, verifying the hypothesis for prime descent.
needed_assertion.objects: Pi and Pi^sigma are cuspidal GL2 forms over L attached to conjugate restrictions of the same global r.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: Each generator sigma at a downward prime step.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: Global r identifies the conjugate Galois restrictions. U04 compares their unramified arithmetic polynomials; the common weight normalizes them to the same unitary Hecke classes.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: Same field L and total dimension 2.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Apply separately at every step to the corrected form attached to r.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not infer invariance of an arbitrary intermediate descendant merely from invariance of its base change.
needed_assertion.constants: Both exceptional Hecke sets are finite.
needed_assertion.normalization: Conjugate primes have equal residue cardinalities, so arithmetic-to-unitary scaling preserves equality.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Compare attached representations, compare Hecke data, apply multiplicity one, then invoke prime descent.

comparisons.comparison: Pi and Pi^sigma are representations over the same L.
Take both Levi groups to be GL2 itself in (2.4).
Both forms are cuspidal, as required.
Global conjugation of r gives equality at all but finitely many primes, not just primes split over K.
Residue norms are preserved by sigma, so unitary Hecke classes agree.
Conjugacy of the full-GL2 cuspidal pairs is isomorphism of the two forms.
That is the exact invariance hypothesis of III4.2(d).
Jacquet-Shalika and Shahidi inputs named in III2 remain published theorem premises, not new proofs here.
The same comparison is repeated after every finite-character correction.
